resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Arabic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Arabic pass identified 25 actionable formula, unit, terminology, and technical-clarity defects across electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, and heat-flux content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Arabic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The Ohm-law voltage conclusion spelled out the unit without retaining the protected symbol.
evidence: The previous conclusion was ‘الجهد هو 5 فولت.’
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘الجهد هو 5 فولت (5 V).’

findings.summary: The Joule-heating power formula localized the protected watt unit into Arabic text.
evidence: The previous expression ended with ‘7.2 واط’.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected W unit.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating conclusion mixed spelled-out units and inconsistent time notation.
evidence: The previous conclusion used ‘جول في الثانية’ and ‘72 جول خلال 10 ثوانٍ’.
findings.resolution: Normalized the result to 7.2 W, 72 J, and 10 s.

findings.summary: The parallel-resistance current formula localized V, Ω, and A into inconsistent Arabic unit words.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘I_total = 4.0 فولت / 0.20 أوم = 20 أ’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘I_total = 4.0 V / 0.20 Ω = 20 A’.

findings.summary: The parallel-branch conclusion used the ambiguous Arabic abbreviation أ for ampere.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended with ‘10 أ’.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected A symbol.

findings.summary: The sine formula used English side labels in the Arabic presentation.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Changed the labels to ‘المقابل / الوتر’.

findings.summary: The cosine formula used English side labels in the Arabic presentation.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘adjacent / hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Changed the labels to ‘المجاور / الوتر’.

findings.summary: The tangent formula used English side labels in the Arabic presentation.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / adjacent’.
findings.resolution: Changed the labels to ‘المقابل / المجاور’.

findings.summary: The worked sine formula retained the English word opposite.
evidence: The previous expression began ‘opposite =’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Arabic label المقابل.

findings.summary: The worked cosine formula retained the English word adjacent.
evidence: The previous expression began ‘adjacent =’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Arabic label المجاور.

findings.summary: The inverse-sine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘المقابل / الوتر’.

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘adjacent / hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘المجاور / الوتر’.

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / adjacent’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘المقابل / المجاور’.

findings.summary: The degrees-to-radians formula used the English unit word radians.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘180° = π radians’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Arabic unit name راديان.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity variable definition omitted Q and described the unit relationship unclearly.
evidence: The previous bullet was ‘يتم نقل الطاقة الحرارية بالجول (J).’
findings.resolution: Defined Q explicitly as transferred thermal energy in joules.

findings.summary: The mass unit was written as a spaced colloquial form and the c definition lacked clear unit phrasing.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘كيلو جرام’.
findings.resolution: Standardized the wording to الكيلوغرام and J/(kg·K).

findings.summary: The heat-capacity worked formula localized Q and J into Arabic letters.
evidence: The previous expression began ‘س =’ and ended with ‘ج’.

findings.summary: The heating-time formula localized t, J, W, and s into prose words or Arabic letters.
evidence: The previous expression began ‘ر =’ and used ‘جول’ and ‘وات’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘t = 41,800 J / 100 W = 418 s’.

findings.summary: The heating-time conclusion used a less precise time noun and omitted the protected seconds symbol.
evidence: The previous conclusion used ‘الوقت المثالي’ and ‘523 ثانية’.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it with الزمن and the protected s unit.

findings.summary: The heat-flux definition used an awkward Arabic clause for heat crossing a surface.
evidence: The previous sentence ended with ‘المعدل الذي تعبر به الحرارة السطح’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the clear construction ‘معدل عبور الحرارة للسطح’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example title omitted the technical concept of flux density.
evidence: The previous title was ‘متوسط تدفق السخان’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘متوسط كثافة تدفق الحرارة من سخان’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example conclusion used spelled-out units and omitted thousands grouping.
evidence: The previous conclusion used ‘5000 واط/م²’ and ‘0.5 واط/سم²’.
findings.resolution: Normalized it to 5,000 W/m² and 0.5 W/cm².

findings.summary: The practical heat-flux bullet was a fragment rather than an instruction.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘وتشمل مقاومة الاتصال’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the direct imperative ‘أدرج مقاومة التلامس ...’.

findings.summary: The final heat-flux check used infinitives and lacked a clear distinction between rate and temperature.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘استخدام السعة الحرارية لتغيير درجة الحرارة’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a direct reminder to use heat capacity for temperature change.

findings.summary: The heat-flux worked formula localized W, m², and W/m² into Arabic unit words.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘وات’ and ‘م²’ in the formula body.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected expression ‘q'' = 100 W / 0.020 m² = 5,000 W/m²’.
